definition: Unsustainable means unable to be continued at the same rate or level.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word unsustainable. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know unsustainable should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Accountants ruled the club's wage bill unsustainable: player salaries swallowed every ticket, shirt, and television dollar, with nothing left for the stadium loan.
A punishing schedule hurts but can be endured — people keep punishing schedules for decades; unsustainable adds the deadline: this one has an expiry.
Ruinous overtakes unsustainable: the unsustainable budget will fail someday, while the ruinous one is wrecking the household now, invoice by invoice.

Untenable is about defense: a position — an argument, a policy, a military line — that cannot be held once real pressure arrives. Unsustainable is about arithmetic: a rate that cannot be continued, whatever anyone argues about it. An untenable claim collapses under questioning; an unsustainable budget collapses on schedule.

Excessive scolds the amount: more than is needed, wanted, or proper, judged right now. It is a verdict about size, not about time. Unsustainable is a verdict about trajectory — the amount might be exactly what is needed, and the rate still cannot be kept up.
